author: Thoughty2
description:
At just 47 miles long, the Panama Railroad wasn’t exactly what you’d call an epic distance. And yet, building it proved so spectacularly difficult that around 12,000 poor souls lost their lives in the process. 

Carving a railway through dense jungle, disease-ridden swamps and relentless tropical downpours wasn’t so much a feat of engineering, but more like extreme combat with nature.

When it finally opened in 1855, those 47 miles revolutionised global trade, slashing journey times between the Atlantic and Pacific and proving that sometimes the shortest stretch of railway can have the biggest impact.
title: The Railway Built Through Hell
